jobs.title: Audio-Visual Intern at Gordon Research Conferences
jobs.description: Employer: Gordon Research Conferences Expires: 11/22/2026 Audio-Visual Intern Experience the excitement behind the scenes of global scientific conferences.Gordon Research Conferences is a nonprofit organization with a prestigious reputation for creating enduring scientific communities that advance the frontiers of research in biology, chemistry, physics, engineering, and related technologies. The conferences bring a global network of scientists together to discuss the latest pre-publication research in their field. There are over 400 Gordon Research Conferences (GRCs) and Gordon Research Seminars (GRSs) per year. At Gordon Research Conferences, gain hands-on event management experience, and help create spaces where groundbreaking discoveries are discussed. Housing and meals are provided, and every week brings a new scientific community, new challenges, and new connections.As an Audio-Visual Intern, you will manage the audio-visual equipment in the meeting room, including sound and projection equipment, and you will deliver exceptional customer service, apply organizational policies, and support GRC's mission of advancing the frontiers of science through global scientific collaboration. ResponsibilitiesAudio-Visual SupportOperate audio, video, and presentation equipment (such as, soundboard, microphones, projector and switchboard) during events and handle equipment challenges in a timely and professional manner.Meet with conferees on site to assist with presenter setup, including microphone placement and laptop configuration, to ensure the equipment setup is working properly.Set up and break down audio-visual equipment, while maintaining, cleaning, and properly storing equipment after each use.Customer ExperienceInterpret and communicate organizational policies and procedures, ensuring consistent application while fostering positive experiences for attendees and chairs.Serve as the primary point of contact in the meeting room for conference and seminar chairs, and community members, fostering strong relationships and ensuring the successful execution of events.Provide responsive, high-quality customer service by addressing inquiries, resolving issues, and communicating effectively with conferees, venue staff, and GRC headquarters.Monitor attendance levels in the room and ensure all conferees are wearing badges in accordance with registration requirements.CollaborationWork closely with headquarters staff to support conference success, maintaining consistent communication with your management to provide timely updates and escalate issues, concerns, or time-sensitive information. Partner with the Event Operations and Logistics Interns to ensure weekly documentation is provided, and slides needed are shared prior to the event taking place. Provide coverage for the Event Operations and Logistics Interns, as necessary.Maintain consistent communication with your manager, providing a weekly report, timely updates, and escalating issues, concerns, or time-sensitive information as appropriate. Required QualificationsExcellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build relationships and communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders.Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with sound judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.Strong PC skills including knowledge of Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Keynote, and Google Slides.Experience with audio visual equipment such as projectors, sound boards, and microphones is preferred, but not required.Familiarity with Windows and Mac operating systems, and knowledge of adjusting display settings for both platforms.Ability to quickly and calmly solve equipment malfunctions as they may arise. Why Join GRC?Build professional skills in event management, customer service, leadership, and technology.Network with scientists, researchers, and professionals from around the world.Live and work on-site with a close-knit team.Housing and meals provided throughout the conference season.Gain experience that strengthens graduate school, nonprofit, event management, and professional career applications.Contribute to conferences that support scientific breakthroughs and global collaboration.Competitive hourly pay and a unique experience unlike a traditional office job.

activities and maintain accurate engineering records. • Support foundry transfer projects and process qualification activities. • Assist with data mining, trend analysis, and engineering database activities. • Help organize engineering documentation, qualification reports, and project records. • Assist with cross-functional communication between internal teams and external foundries.Required written communication skills.Preferred Qualifications • Coursework or experience in semiconductor manufacturing, microelectronics, or IC fabrication. • Basic knowledge of semiconductor processes and device physics. • Experience with data analysis and statistical methods. • Python programming experience is highly desirable. • Familiarity with scripting, automation, or data visualization tools is a plus. • Experience with JMP, MATLAB, SQL, or similar analytical tools is beneficial.Learning Opportunities During this internship, the student will gain exposure to: • Semiconductor wafer fabrication processes. • Process Control Monitoring (PCM) methodologies. • Foundry management and supplier interactions. • Yield improvement and process qualification activities. • Engineering lot management and production monitoring. • Cross-functional collaboration with Manufacturing, Product, Test, and NPI teams. • Data analytics and automation within a semiconductor manufacturing environment.Preferred Skills: • Electrical Engineering background required. • Python programming experience preferred. • Ability to analyze large datasets and identify process trends. • Strong organizational and record-keeping capabilities. • Interest in semiconductor manufacturing and foundry operations.This internship offers an excellent opportunity to gain practical experience in semiconductor manufacturing and external foundry engineering while working directly with experienced engineers on real production and qualification programs.During the 12 weeks each Intern will: • Be given an individual and well-defined project with set outcome goals • Gain hands on experience • Receive excellent training and ongoing supervision • Be invited to attend an intern webinar series • Attend networking/social events • Attend and present at Poster Session about each Interns project successes and pitfalls • Receive formal, written feedbackThe Hourly Range for this position is $20 – $47 per hour. jobs.description: Employer: GlobalFoundries Expires: 11/23/2026 About GlobalFoundries GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com. Internship Program Overview: Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. Summary of Role: Join the New Product Development team for a hands-on engineering internship focused on automated test solutions for complex digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in automotive and industrial applications. You will work alongside Product and Test Engineers on defined assignments spanning test planning, ATE development, silicon bring-up, validation, data analysis, and manufacturing-readiness activities using Advantest and Teradyne platforms. Essential Responsibilities include: Support pre-silicon planning by translating product requirements and datasheets into technical specifications, specification-compliance matrices, design-for-test requirements, and ATE test plans. Assist with the design of cost-effective ATE hardware and resource allocation that improve multisite efficiency and pin multiplexing for silicon bring-up, validation, and production release. Develop, bring up, validate, and debug automated test programs for digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits on Advantest and Teradyne ATE platforms. Analyze test and characterization data to investigate design margins, wafer-fabrication process variation, parametric performance, yield, and test-time opportunities. Support process-window experiments, silicon and package qualification activities, and product specification compliance across automotive, industrial, or commercial requirements. Collaborate with Design, DFT, Design Validation, Program Management, Quality and Reliability Engineering, Customer Quality Engineering, Bench Characterization, Applications, Fab, Assembly, and factory Test teams. Contribute to ATE test hardware, socket design, board schematics, layout, diagnostic code, and test automation specifications under the guidance of experienced engineers. Document gaps, lessons learned, and best practices, and contribute reusable methods to the Standard Test Methods Library (STML) across ATE platforms. Other Responsibilities: Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications: Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship. jobs.description: Employer: GlobalFoundries Expires: 11/23/2026 About GlobalFoundries GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity, and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com. New College Graduates Overview: We offer many full-time employment paths for recent graduates, which provide accelerated training in a fast-paced work environment, cross-functional working opportunities, and talent mobility. New college graduates are provided with mentorship, networking, and leadership opportunities, which give our new team members life-long connections and skills. Summary of Role: Join the New Product Development team as an early-career Test Engineer responsible for developing and productizing cost-effective automated test solutions for complex digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in automotive and industrial applications. You will contribute across the full product lifecycle, from pre-silicon test strategy through silicon bring-up, qualification, manufacturing release, yield improvement, and cost reduction on Advantest and Teradyne ATE platforms. Essential Responsibilities include: Support pre-silicon planning by translating product requirements and datasheets into technical specifications, specification-compliance matrices, design-for-test requirements, and ATE test plans. Assist with the design of cost-effective ATE hardware and resource allocation that improve multisite efficiency and pin multiplexing for silicon bring-up, validation, and production release. Develop, bring up, validate, and debug automated test programs for digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits on Advantest and Teradyne ATE platforms. Analyze test and characterization data to investigate design margins, wafer-fabrication process variation, parametric performance, yield, and test-time opportunities. Support process-window experiments, silicon and package qualification activities, and product specification compliance across automotive, industrial, or commercial requirements. Collaborate with Design, DFT, Design Validation, Program Management, Quality and Reliability Engineering, Customer Quality Engineering, Bench Characterization, Applications, Fab, Assembly, and factory Test teams. Contribute to ATE test hardware, socket design, board schematics, layout, diagnostic code, and test automation specifications under the guidance of experienced engineers. Document gaps, lessons learned, and best practices, and contribute reusable methods to the Standard Test Methods Library (STML) across ATE platforms. Own assigned products from silicon bring-up through manufacturing release, drive product-entitlement targets and critical ramp metrics, and support test-time, yield, burn-in, and manufacturing-flow improvements. Other Responsibilities: Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications: Education – Graduating with a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field from an accredited degree program. Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and proven good academic standing. Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal) Experience in semiconductor test, design-for-test (DFT), or integrated-circuit design. Proficiency in one or more programming languages, including C, C++, Python, or Perl. Preferred Qualifications: Prior related internship or co-op experience. Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc. Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making. Project management skills, i.e. the ability to innovate and execute solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity. Strong written and verbal communication skills Strong planning & organizational skills Experience with Advantest or Teradyne ATE platforms. Knowledge of ATE architecture and experience developing low-level test code. Experience testing digital, analog, or mixed-signal integrated circuits. Experience with silicon characterization, qualification, or manufacturing ramp. Familiarity with applicable automotive, industrial, or commercial semiconductor qualification standards. #NCGProgramUS Expected Salary Range$86,000.00 - $148,000.00The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location.If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please contact us by email at usaccommodations@gf.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Our team is composed of dedicated professionals who are passionate about making a positive impact. We are on a mission to challenge, inspire, and teach technology skills to students, particularly those from refugee and underserved backgrounds. (Willingness to learn)What we offer: Flexible Schedule averaging to 10 hours/weekMix of remote and on-site workCasual dress codePurpose-driven culture Overview of the Tech Mentorship Program:The Pi515 Tech Mentorship Program runs from September to March, offering high school students the opportunity to learn how to code using Python. jobs.description: Employer: Alliance Laundry Systems, LLC Expires: 11/24/2026 Join Our Team as a Supplier Quality Engineering Co-op! Timing/Duration of Internship/Co-op: Spring/Summer 2027 Co-Op (January to August) or, Summer/Fall 2027 Co-Op (May to December))Ripon, WI — on-site, 1st shift. Most of what goes into a finished product is made by someone else. Do you want to learn how a company makes sure those parts are right — and what happens when they are not? Join our Supplier Quality team in Ripon, WI, as a Supplier Quality Engineering Co-op. Working alongside our Supplier Quality Engineers, you will help qualify new parts, support investigations into supplier issues, and see how a supply base is managed. Why Join Us? Broad Exposure: Support part qualification, supplier audits, and corrective action work across multiple commodities. Real-World Impact: Contribute to qualifications and investigations that continue after your term ends. Professional Development: Learn PPAP, APQP, supplier auditing, and root cause investigation from engineers who do it every day. Supplier quality runs on timelines that do not fit in a summer. A co-op term is long enough to follow those cycles from start to close. Apply now. Your Role: Support the qualification of assigned parts or a commodity group, including helping prepare and review PPAP submissions. Help track open supplier quality issues and assist the team in following them through to resolution. Assist with investigations into non-conforming material, supporting root cause analysis and the documentation of Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCARs). Participate in supplier audits and technical reviews alongside your mentor, observing how quality systems and process capability are evaluated. Help compile supplier KPIs such as defects per million and on-time delivery, and prepare reject and warranty summaries for the management team. Support APQP activities and assist Design and Manufacturing Engineering with clarifying component specifications and tolerances. Blueprint reading ability, or readiness to learn it quickly, including the ability to interpret standards such as ASTM. Functional understanding of statistics as applied to quality, or coursework underway. Strong computer skills, including Excel; familiarity with SAP, Minitab, or Power BI is a plus. Willingness to ask questions and seek direction from your mentor and the broader Quality team. Education: Currently pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or Supply Chain, with sophomore standing or above, and eligible for a multi-term co-op through your school. This work will investigate improvements in data preprocessing, model architecture, training strategies, and hyperparameter selection while comparing AI-driven research with conventional experimentation in terms of model performance, reproducibility, and research efficiency.The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong eagerness to learn and grow professionally and possess excellent communication skills—both written and verbal. jobs.title: DTRA Kinetic Technology Systems Modeling, Testing and Analysis Fellowship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/26/2026 The Test Support Division, Test Science Branch, of the Research and Development Directorate for the Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) is offering a master's/doctoral level fellowship opportunity in kinetic weapons technology. What will I be doing and why should I apply?DTRA-West offers a distinctly unique experience for research-based experiences, professional development, and future career opportunities for selected fellows and interns, not to mention the beauty of Albuquerque and the surrounding area. As a selected candidate, you will engage with researchers and engineers within the DTRA complex and be a part of, and witness to, objective evaluations and assessments of new capabilities aimed at countering WMD and emerging threats. Albuquerque is New Mexico’s largest city, where the modern city skyline is set against a backdrop of the stunning Sandia Mountains and an endless, timeless blue sky. Albuquerque boasts a unique multicultural history and heritage. Native American, Hispanic & Latino cultural influences are a part of everyday life.As an Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) participant, you will join and learn from a community of scientists and researchers engaged in planning and accomplishing research projects in the Test Support Division, Test Science Branch at DTRA. You will participate in kinetic and other weapons testing at White Sands Missile Range, Kirtland Air-Force Base, and other test sites.Why should I apply? Under the guidance of a mentor, you will:Learn how to research issues and conduct feasibility studies pertaining to the engineering and scientific elements of prospective projects/testsUnderstand how to design and develop test plans and analysis methodologies through participation in test teamsLearn presentation techniques incorporating information related to kinetic and/or non-kinetic weapons effectsGain experience with diagnostic instrumentation development, gauge ranging, and analyzing test dataLearn how to evaluate test results and document findingsDevelop ability to participate effectively in Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMS) with customers, technical personnel, and contractors to gather technical requirements from all partiesWithin one year, you will gain significant knowledge and experience related to the modeling and analysis of weapons systems interactions with targets and the response and damage of targets to weapons effects. Where will I be located?Albuquerque, New MexicoWhat is the anticipated start date?The Test Support Division, Test Science Branch at DTRA is ready to make appointments immediately. Exact start dates will be determined at the time of selection and in coordination with the selected candidate. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis and internships or fellowships will be filled as qualified candidates are identified.What is the appointment length?This appointment is a full-time, twelve-month research appointment, with the possibility to be renewed for additional research periods. Appointments may be extended depending on funding availability, project assignment, program rules, and availability of the participant. What are the provisions?You will receive a stipend to be determined by DTRA. Stipends are typically based on a participant’s academic standing, discipline, experience, and research facility location. The anticipated stipend range for this opportunity is $5400-$5800 per month based on full-time participation.Other provisions may include the following:Health Insurance Supplement (Participants are eligible to purchase health insurance through ORISE)Relocation/Dislocation AllowanceTraining and Travel AllowanceAbout DTRAThe Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and its allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict. This opportunity is within the Research and Development Directorate of DTRA, Test and Assessment Department. For more information about the DTRA, please visit https://www.dtra.mil/. About ORISEThis program, administered by Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU) through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and DoD. Participants do not enter into an employee/employer relationship with ORISE, ORAU, DoD or any other office or agency. Instead, you will be affiliated with ORISE for the administration of the appointment through the ORISE appointment letter and Terms of Appointment. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE. For more information, visit the ORISE Research Participation Program at the U.S. Department of Defense.

jobs.description: Employer: Procter & Gamble (P&G) Expires: 11/26/2026 Research and Development (R&D) at Procter & Gamble, the largest consumer packaged goods company in the world, includes a diverse group of roles that contribute to the innovation and development of our products. It encompasses roles in product research, formulation, testing, and scientific analysis. You will find variety and excitement starting Day 1. This internship is specifically designed for individuals working towards a PhD who are developing proficiency in their field. As an intern or co-op in management, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals in a supportive environment. This is a 12-week paid internship, designed to provide you with a solid foundation for future career growth. The internship will take place from May (potentially early June) to August of 2027. Join us at P&G, where your contributions will play a vital role in shaping the future of consumer products! The Opportunity:P&G has an opportunity for a PhD intern to work in our Corporate Function R&D area. In this internship you will explore how computational modeling and simulation can provide deeper insight into the molecular mechanisms that govern material behavior. Working at the intersection of polymer physics, computational science, and materials innovation, you will investigate whether molecular and multiscale modeling approaches can explain observed material performance, generate new structure-property hypotheses, and enable more intentional materials design.The project offers the opportunity to collaborate with both experimental scientists and computational modelers. By the end of the internship, you will have assessed whether modern simulation and theoretical tools can serve as practical design capabilities for accelerating materials innovation and reducing dependence on trial-and-error experimentation. Key Responsibilities:Evaluate computational approaches relevant to polymer science, soft materials, and molecular modelingApply simulation and theoretical methods to representative polymer systemsDevelop and execute demonstration simulations using multiscale modeling approachesCompare model predictions with experimental observations and technical design needsCreate scripts and workflows for simulation setup, execution, and analysisAssess whether modeling can generate new design hypotheses, improve material selection, or reduce experimental iterationDocument findings and present recommendations to technical partners Job QualificationsRequired Qualifications:Education: Working towards a PhD in Polymer Science, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Computational Chemistry, Soft Matter Physics, or related discipline.Experience in polymer physics, soft materials, molecular simulation, molecular dynamics, coarse-grained modeling, computational chemistry, or multiscale materials modeling.Programming experience in Python is required. Experience with molecular simulation packages, such as LAMMPS or similar tools, would be particularly relevant.Familiarity with the mechanical behavior of soft materials (e.g., dynamic mechanical analysis and tensile testing).Available to work a 12-week internship from May/early June to August in the summer of 2027. This is an in-person internship; candidate is expected to work from our Mason Business Center 3-5 days a week. Preferred Qualifications:Basic understanding of polymer synthesis methods and standard chemistry laboratory practices.Experience working with film-forming materials would be valuable. Mobility is a key component of many management careers, providing opportunities to grow through different assignments, locations, and business challenges. Candidates should be prepared to consider relocation opportunities throughout their career as business needs and development opportunities arise. jobs.title: Signal Integrity Engineer Intern at MACOM
jobs.description: Employer: MACOM Expires: 11/27/2026 MACOM (NASDAQ: MTSI) is a global leader in the design and manufacture of advanced semiconductor products across a diverse range of end markets, including Data Centers, Telecommunications, Industrial and Aerospace and Defense. We develop innovative, cutting-edge technologies and products across the spectrum of radio frequency (RF), microwave, millimeter wave, photonics and high-speed analog technologies. Our solutions support critical network infrastructure applications like artificial intelligence, high performance computing, satellite communications, radar, unmanned aerial vehicles, medical equipment, test and measurement and advanced wireless networks.MACOM has more than 75 years of expertise in semiconductor process development, wafer fabrication, circuit design, advanced packaging, systems architecture and applications engineering. We are committed to our customers’ success. We partner with customers to help solve their most challenging problems by providing semiconductor solutions that are at the forefront of the highest power, highest frequency and/or highest data rates.Leading technologies, innovative products and driven employees. Come be a part of MACOM and help advance the next generation of connectivity infrastructure!Signal Integrity Engineer InternJoin our engineering team and help develop the high-speed hardware that powers next-generation networking, computing, and communications systems. As a Signal Integrity Engineer Intern, you will work with experienced engineers to analyze, simulate, and validate high-speed channels, interconnects, PCBs, and packages to ensure reliable performance.You will support signal integrity investigations through modeling, simulation, and laboratory measurements, using industry-standard tools and test equipment. Key responsibilities include analyzing S-parameter data, evaluating channel performance, troubleshooting signal quality issues, and collaborating with hardware, PCB, and product development teams.Candidates should be pursuing a Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field, with coursework in electromagnetics, transmission lines, or high-speed digital design. Strong analytical skills, curiosity, and a passion for solving complex engineering challenges are essential. Experience with SI simulation tools such as HFSS, VNAs, and Python-based data analysis is a plus.During the 12 weeks each Intern will:• Be given an individual and well-defined project with set outcome goals• Gain hands on experience• Receive excellent training and ongoing supervision• Be invited to attend an intern webinar series• Attend networking/social events• Attend and present at Poster Session about each Interns project successes and pitfalls• Receive formal, written feedbackThe Hourly Range for this position is $20 – $47 per hour. Actual salary offered to candidate will depend on several factors, including but not limited to, work location, relevant candidates’ experience, education, and specific knowledge, skills, and abilities.EEO:MACOM is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to a diverse workforce. MACOM will not discriminate against any worker or job applicant on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, military service, marital status, or any other category protected under applicable law.Reasonable Accommodation:MACOM is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with physical and mental disabilities. If you have a disability and are in need of a reasonable accommodation with respect to any part of the application process please call +1-978-656-2500 or email HR_Ops@MACOM.com. Provide your name, phone number and the position title and location in which you are interested, and nature of accommodation needed, and we will get back to you. We also work with current employees who request or need reasonable accommodation in order to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

jobs.description: Employer: Marine Solutions Expires: 11/28/2026 WHO WE AREAre you a driven and aspiring civil engineering student looking to gain hands-on experience in the field? Join our team as a Civil Engineering Intern in our Salt Lake City, Utah, office for summer 2027 and embark on an exciting journey to learn and contribute to real-world projects. You will work closely with our experienced engineers, gaining practical insights into the world of civil engineering while assisting in various project tasks. This internship will provide you with valuable exposure to the infrastructure and construction industry.Marine Solutions is a specialized marine engineering and construction firm serving clients in the government (federal, state, local), transportation, energy, industrial, water, and commercial markets. We inspect, design, and build bridges and waterfront infrastructure worldwide that protect and enrich our communities.Our recognition as one of the Best Places to Work in Kentucky for nine consecutive years reflects our unwavering commitment to nurturing and empowering our people. We prioritize personal and professional development, providing opportunities for continuous learning and growth. Collaboration and open communication are at the core of our culture, fostering a supportive and inclusive environment where every individual's voice is valued. Investing in our employees not only enhances their potential but also contributes to our collective success. SUMMARY OF POSITIONEngineering Intern duties include but are not limited to assisting with various engineering tasks and assignments such as preparing for and conducting field inspections, data reduction, reporting, engineering analyses, and design. Work is performed under the direction of a Project Engineer or higher who makes assignments, provides guidance, and reviews work to ensure that it is completed according to instructions and in accordance with accepted principles and practices of civil engineering. Additional duties and responsibilities may be assigned or modified at any time. YOU WILL NEEDExcellent communication skills (verbal and written) in the English language. Ability to define problems, collect/interpret data, evaluate facts, draw valid conclusions, and effectively communicate findings/results. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage tasks efficiently and effectively. EDUCATION & EXPERIENCEHigher-level mathematics, including trigonometry, algebra, geometry, and calculus, and its application to surveying and engineering computations.0-4 years of relevant experience.MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSPossess knowledge of current literature, trends, and developments in the field of engineering and the ability to keep current with new developments.Possess knowledge of construction practices (concrete, steel, carpentry, welding, etc.).Proficient in technical writing.Proficient in basic computer functions (Microsoft Office, etc.).Be a self-starter and able to work as independently as possible.Current medical certifications including bloodborne pathogens, first aid, CPR, and emergency oxygen administration if performing fieldwork.Possess Marine Solutions core values including integrity, teamwork, dependability, and going above and beyond.PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONSCurriculum focus in structural or geotechnical engineeringAutoCAD proficiencyEngineering software experiencePHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, WORK ENVIRONMENT & SAFETYThe duties of this position require the intern to regularly sit, stand, walk, use hands, reach with hands and arms, and talk and hear. This position requires maintaining current industry knowledge and expertise through active involvement in professional organizations and/or other activities that may require additional and/or flexible working hours. jobs.description: Employer: Vals AI Expires: 11/28/2026 About the RoleWe are looking for exceptional engineers to join our team as interns.You, alongside our team, will work on the platform that runs our benchmarks. This spans everything needed to evaluate LLMs at scale: Python libraries, a web platform, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and tooling. You'll work across the stack—whatever needs to be built to run benchmarks reliably and efficiently.At Vals, we believe in autonomy. You will be given a high degree of independence to make decisions on tech stacks, system architecture, and code structure. You will also provide guidance to others on the team, both through informal feedback and formal processes like architecture and code reviews while learning from our team of full-time engineers and researchers. Our platform serves startups, enterprises, and research labs measuring model performance. We work with all the major foundation model labs, and some of the largest financial institutions and hospital systems in the world. jobs.description: Employer: Andersen Corporation Expires: 11/28/2026 ANDERSEN CORPORATION SUMMARY:At Andersen, we see possibility everywhere, every day and in everything we do. The possibility for our employees to achieve their full potential, for our communities to be stronger and for everyone to have a healthier, happier place to live.Our portfolio of brands — Andersen Windows & Doors, Renewal by Andersen and Fenetres MQ — is crafted to serve customers across the new residential, home improvement and light commercial building sector.Join our more than 13,000 employees who are inspired every day to deliver exceptional experiences that turn possibility into reality.JOB DESCRIPTION:Positions may be in Garland, TX, Goodyear, AZ, Bayport, MN, or Cottage Grove, MN.POSITION SUMMARY: Supply chain process improvements and support. Position may cover areas in manufacturing or distribution such as demand planning, resource planning, purchased material planning, scheduling, material flow, information flow, inventory management, and/or transportation planning.POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES:Facilitate cross-functional teams having explicit objectives and scopePropose, implement, and support business tool and process enhancementsPerform data analyses to support recommendationsEnsure new processes integrate with existing processes.Train customers on new and modified processes. Opportunities may Include:Utilize lean tools to lead and direct continuous improvement activitiesDefine problems, collect and analyze dataRecommend and implement effective solutionsImprove material or information flow within a plant or distribution centerLead Time ImprovementsRaw or finished goods inventory ManagementTransportation process improvementsMetrics programs for internal or external suppliers Preferred Qualifications:Obtaining bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing technology, Industrial Engineering, Management Informational Systems (MIS) COMPENSATION: Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to work experience, education, geographic location, certifications, etc. Your recruiter can share more about the specific compensation package for your preferred role during the hiring process. Successful candidates in this role are expected to earn $22 - $27.*DISCLAIMER: Interns are not eligible for benefits.PAY RANGE:CULTURE AND BENEFITS:At Andersen, we believe our people are at the heart of everything we do. Every day, their talent, dedication and passion enables us to be the most trusted window & door company. To support our employees, we provide a comprehensive Total Rewards Package – a thoughtful combination of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to investing in each team member’s wellbeing and success. While specific benefits may vary by position or location, we’re proud to offer a comprehensive Total Rewards Package designed to support your well‑being, growth, and future. Our benefits include:401 (k) Plan, Employer Fixed Contributions & Company MatchingProfit Sharing*Medical, Dental and Vision Coverage*Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs)*, Health Savings Account (HSA) and Health Reimbursement Account (HRA)Life InsurancePaid Time Off & Paid HolidaysPaid Maternity Leave & Paid Parental Leave*Career Growth Planning & Nationwide Career Opportunities*For employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement, some benefits may differ or may not be available based on the terms of the agreement.PROFIT SHARING: In 2026 Andersen has set a profit-sharing target of $3,600 per eligible employee, prorated as appropriate. Profit Sharing will be paid out in quarterly installments to provide eligible employees with payments throughout the year, with payment amounts tied to quarterly operating profit performance.EEOC EMPLOYER: Andersen is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, disability, marital status, national origin, citizenship, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Andersen Corporation will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable federal, state and local laws.If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, participate in a job interview, or engage in any part of the hiring process, please contact HRCompliance@andersencorp.com.We look forward to seeing how your unique skills, background and experiences will inspire our team and help us continue to be the leader we are today.

jobs.title: EHS (Environmental Health & Safety) Intern - Summer 2027 at James Hardie Building Products
jobs.description: Employer: James Hardie Building Products Expires: 11/28/2026 Internship ObjectiveGain hands-on experience in Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) by supporting process improvement initiatives, documentation management, and site safety programs within a manufacturing environment. The intern will develop technical, analytical, and communication skills while helping create accurate, organized, and sustainable EHS resources that support compliance and operational excellence.By the end of the internship, the intern will update and field-verify facility and emergency response maps, identify and document EHS improvement opportunities, track corrective actions to completion or ownership assignment, and present a final summary of project outcomes, recommendations, and opportunities for continued improvement. The internship will provide a strong foundation in manufacturing EHS practices, hazard identification, and cross-functional collaboration.What You'll Do:Internship ResponsibilitiesReview and update facility line drawings, fire extinguisher maps, evacuation routes, severe weather maps, and emergency equipment locations.Assist with environmental compliance activities, including chemical inventories, waste inspections, spill-prevention readiness, stormwater reviews, and recordkeepingCollaborate with EHS team members to ensure training materials reflect current policies, procedures, and best practices.What You'll Bring:Currently enrolled in a bachelor's degree program in a relevant discipline at an accredited university, with an anticipated graduation date between December 2027 and May 2029 (rising junior or rising senior).Strong academic performance with a minimum GPA of 3.0.Available to work full-time for 12 weeks during summer 2027.Reliable transportation to and from the work location.Authorization to work in the United States. Preferred SkillsTarget major: pursuing degree in OESH/Environmental Science/Industrial Hygiene, Environmental ScienceProficiency with Microsoft Office, even AutoCAD may be helpful.Effective written and verbal communication skillsComfortable spending time on the production floor and engaging with plant operations.What You’ll Receive:As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay scale for this position is $20 to $25 per hour. Placement in the range depends on several factors such as experience, skills, geography and may change over time.Full-time work experience and competitive payMeaningful projects with business impactMentorship and guidanceFeedback and evaluationExposure to James Hardie cultureNetworking opportunities and skill developmentEEO: James Hardie Building Products Inc. is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, gender, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, genetic information, veteran's status, marital status, pregnancy, disability, or any other basis protected by law. James Hardie will comply with any applicable state and local laws regarding employee leave benefits, including, but not limited to providing time off pursuant to the Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, in accordance with its plans and policies. The position responsibilities outlined above are in no way to be construed as all encompassing. Other duties, responsibilities, and qualifications may be required and/or assigned as necessary.
